content_of_post_to_comment:
Tried grayscale last Monday because everyone says it kills the dopamine. Notifications looked dead, which was nice. Didn’t stop my thumb.

I’d unlock to check the time, and somehow I’d still land in Instagram. Black and white didn’t matter. The icon wasn’t even colorful anymore and I still tapped it.

What actually slowed me down was putting the phone in a drawer while I cooked dinner. Not a whole “digital detox.” Just one meal. First night I checked the drawer twice. Second night once. By Thursday I finished cooking without thinking about it.

Grayscale is still on. Not because I’m cured. Because when I do open something dumb, it looks slightly worse and I leave faster. Small win.

Not selling anything. Just what stuck after the grayscale advice alone didn’t.
comment: The drawer experiment makes a lot of sense because it changes the default behavior instead of trying to fight the urge every few minutes. I've noticed the same thing with habits like snacking or checking apps: adding a little friction works better than relying on willpower. Grayscale feels like a reminder, but distance actually breaks the loop.
